newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour repeats vow to replace Camelot.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour repeats vow to replace Camelot.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party on Wednesday reaffirmed its intention to replace Camelot Plc with a "competitive, efficient, not-for-profit operator" of Britain's national lottery when its current contract ends in 2001.
The pledge came in a document on the lottery launched at an election campaign news conference by national heritage spoksesman Jack Cunningham.
The document proposes to create a one billion stg fund for innovative education and health projects from the proceeds of the new midweek lottery draw.
The document says: "When Camelot's current contract runs out in November 2001, Labour will seek a competitive, efficient, not-for-profit operator to ensure that the maximum sums go to good causes.
"The lottery is a monopoly intended to serve the public interest. Labour believes it must be administered efficiently and economically."

Cunningham told the news conference: "People are angry that a private monopoly makes more than one million stg per week profits on their lottery money. Nor should Camelot be allowed to retain millions of pounds of interest on undistributed prize money."
